en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 13.4.
Upādinnattika (The Triplet on Clung-to)

Conditioned by a state that is both grasped and subject to clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*), a state that is neither grasped nor subject to clinging (*naupādinnupādāniya*) arises by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Conditioned by a state that is grasped and subject to clinging, a state that is not un-grasped but subject to clinging (*naanupādinnupādāniya*) arises by way of the root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*), a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging (*na-anupādinnaanupādāniya*) arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, states that are both not acquired and not subject to clinging, as well as states that are neither acquired nor subject to clinging, arise by way of the root condition. Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging...
And states that are neither-clung-to-nor-object-of-clinging arise by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is not-clung-to-but-object-of-clinging, a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-object-of-clinging arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is not-clung-to-but-object-of-clinging, a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-object-of-clinging arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is not-clung-to but subject to clinging, there arise states that are both not-clung-to and subject to clinging, and states that are neither-clung-to nor subject to clinging, by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-clung-to nor subject to clinging, there arises a state that is neither-clung-to nor subject to clinging, by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not acquired by clinging but subject to clinging, by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging, there arises a state that is neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging, there arise both a state that is not acquired by clinging but subject to clinging and a state that is neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging...

And states arise by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-object-of-clinging, there arise states that are both-clung-to-and-object-of-clinging and neither-clung-to-nor-object-of-clinging by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is both-clung-to-and-object-of-clinging and a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-object-of-clinging, [there arises] a state that is not-clung-to-but-object-of-clinging...

A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is not-clung-to-but-favourable-to-clinging and a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-favourable-to-clinging, a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-favourable-to-clinging arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is not-clung-to-but-favourable-to-clinging and a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-favourable-to-clinging, [a state that is] neither-clung-to-nor-favourable-to-clinging... [arises].
And states arise by way of root condition.

Dependent on both acquired-and-object-of-clinging states and unacquired-but-object-of-clinging states, an unacquired-and-not-object-of-clinging state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on both acquired-and-object-of-clinging states and unacquired-but-object-of-clinging states...
A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging arises by way of root-condition dependent on a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging.

Dependent on states that are both-clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging and states that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging, states that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging and states that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging arise by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

Under the root condition (hetu), there are nineteen; under the object condition (ārammaṇa), nine; under the predominance condition (adhipati), eleven ... [and so on] ... under the conascence condition (sahajāta), nineteen ... [and so on] ... under the repetition condition (āsevana), six ... [and so on] ... under the result condition (vipāka), thirteen ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance condition (avigata), nineteen.
(The sections on conascence, conditions, dependence, association, and association-by-connection should also be expanded in detail.
13.4.7. Question Section (Pañhāvāra)

A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is related to a state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is related to a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging by way of the root condition ... [etc. ...
A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is related to a state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging by way of the object condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).

A state that is both acquired (*upādinnupādāniya*) and subject to clinging (*upādāniya*) is a condition for a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging by way of the object-condition.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is [a condition] for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, and for a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging... [by way of the object-condition].

It is a condition by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*). A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition by way of object-condition for a state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging, and for a state that is neither clung-to nor not subject to clinging.
A state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging is a condition by way of object-condition for a state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging.
A state that is not-clung-to-but-favourable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not-clung-to-but-favourable-to-clinging.
A state that is not-clung-to-but-favourable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-favourable-to-clinging.
A state that is not-clung-to-but-favourable-to-clinging [is a condition] for a state that is both not-clung-to-but-favourable-to-clinging and neither-clung-to-nor-favourable-to-clinging...

And a state that is not-clung-to-but-subservient-to-clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not-clung-to-but-subservient-to-clinging and for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-subservient-to-clinging.
A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-subservient-to-clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-subservient-to-clinging … [five] … (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-cause condition, there are thirteen; in object condition, fifteen; in predominance condition, eleven; in proximity condition, sixteen … [and so on] … in conascence condition, nineteen;
in mutuality condition, nine; in dependence condition, twenty-three; in strong-dependence condition, eighteen; in prenascence condition, sixteen;
in postnascence condition, fifteen; in repetition condition, five; in kamma condition, fifteen; in resultant condition, ten; in nutriment condition, twenty; in faculty condition … [and so on].

In the jhāna and path [formulas], there are thirteen; in association, nine; in dissociation, sixteen … pe … in non-disappearance, thirty-six. (The section on questions should also be expanded in detail.)
